title: Polynomial-delay disjointness Gray codes for combinations
formal: For every k≥1 and n≥2k+1 except (n,k)=(5,2), can all k-subsets of [n] be generated in a cyclic disjointness ordering with polynomial delay and polynomial workspace?
definitions: Input is n,k in binary. The output is a list S_0,…,S_(M−1), where M=binomial(n,k), containing every k-subset once, followed by a marked closing copy of S_0. Each output subset is an n-bit characteristic vector; S_i∩S_((i+1) mod M)=∅. One fixed deterministic Turing machine must use at most p(n+k) work bits and at most p(n+k) bit operations before its first output, between completed consecutive outputs, and from the final distinct set to the marked closing copy and termination, for one polynomial p independent of n,k. The write-only output is not counted as workspace and cannot be reread. No exponential preprocessing or advice is allowed. Polynomial here is in n+k, as required by the explicit n-bit output, not in log n.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked construction and proof of all stated guarantees, or a proof that no such construction exists. Existence of a Hamilton cycle or running time polynomial in binomial(n,k) is insufficient.
context: The source proves Hamiltonicity outside the exceptional Petersen case. Its constructive running time is polynomial in the graph size, which may be exponential in n.
